questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
Can a corporation give unlimited money to a super PAC?
questions.why: Since Citizens United and SpeechNow.org (2010), corporations, unions and individuals can give super PACs unlimited sums.

questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
How often do House and Senate campaigns file their regular reports in an election year?
questions.why: Candidate committees file quarterly, plus 12 days before and 30 days after each election. Monthly filing is only an option for PACs and parties.

questions.prompt: Club for Growth Action (a super PAC) has spent $598K in MI's 7th District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Republican or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Republicans have spent $328K in OH's 7th District House race. Are Republicans playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Republicans hold this seat now, so money helping Republicans here is defense.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Republicans have spent $1.2M in MI's 8th District House race. Are Republicans playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Democrats hold this seat now, so money helping Republicans here is offense.

questions.prompt: HMP (a super PAC) has spent $1.8M in MI's 4th District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Democrat or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: What's the most one person can give a House candidate for the 2026 general election?
questions.why: The 2025-26 limit is $3,500 per election; the primary and general each count as separate elections.

questions.prompt: In AZ's 6th District House race, outside money favors Republicans by $710K. Whose nominee has raised more?
questions.why: Outside money and candidate money point opposite ways here: the Democrat leads fundraising by $1.2M.
